name: application_overspeed
description: The fake feedback exceeds runtime.safety.joint_velocity_limits before the runtime leaves Boot, so the lower execution state machine latches JointVelocityExceeded; the real application reports that lower fault in step (behavior=Fault with the lower runtime=Fault, its own cause=RuntimeFault and no target), never claims a stop, and exits bounded and honest - stop=unknown, naming the lower fault, exit 3 - without touching the latched fault. The other half of the lower-fault acceptance, a refused torque write and the single Reset that clears it, is application_fault.

steps.note: the lower layer latches the measured-velocity fault on its own
the upper reports the lower fault in step, with its own cause and no target
the upper never started a move it would have to take back
a latched fault is never cleared, and the application must not be the one to end it
